title: FirstQFM Demonstrates Quantum Reservoir Computing on Rigetti’s 108-Qubit Processor to Outperform Classical Financial Benchmarks - Quantum Computing Report
gist: FirstQFM, with SW7 Group and Rigetti, ran quantum reservoir computing on Rigetti's 108-qubit Cepheus-1-108Q and, in a blinded 43-asset, 600-date out-of-sample test, beat classical ML and Amazon Chronos-2 with 52.02% directional accuracy, 2.12x the P&L of the best baseline and a 1.22 Sharpe. The authors disclaim quantum advantage, noting larger drawdowns and no transaction costs.

insights.claim: FirstQFM's quantum reservoir computing pipeline on Rigetti's Cepheus-1-108Q achieved 52.02% directional accuracy and 0.5176 macro-F1 across 43 anonymized assets and 600 out-of-sample trading dates, ahead of all classical baselines tested.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: One of the more rigorous claimed real-hardware finance results from a NISQ device, relevant to Rigetti's commercial narrative.

insights.claim: On a 43-asset equally weighted portfolio without transaction costs, the QRC system delivered 2.12x the cumulative gross P&L of the best classical baseline (pooled MLP) and an annualized Sharpe ratio of 1.22 versus 0.75 for the MLP.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Edge is reported gross of costs, so investors should discount until net-of-cost performance is shown.
insights.quote: the QRC system achieved 2.12× the cumulative gross P&L of the top classical baseline (pooled MLP) and an annualized Sharpe ratio of 1.22

insights.claim: The QRC model posted positive P&L on 41 of 43 assets, and a historically diversified five-asset sub-portfolio reached a Sharpe ratio of 1.73.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Breadth of positive P&L across assets is a stronger signal than a single aggregate number, though the sub-portfolio selection may be cherry-picked.
insights.quote: A historically diversified five-asset sub-portfolio yielded a Sharpe ratio of 1.73.

insights.claim: Amazon's Chronos-2 time-series foundation model, run zero-shot, delivered the weakest risk-adjusted result among the reported models, with 50.70% accuracy and an annualized Sharpe of 0.39.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Suggests general-purpose time-series foundation models offer little zero-shot edge in financial direction forecasting.

themes.theme: Why reservoir computing suits NISQ hardware

insights.claim: Quantum reservoir computing avoids deep error-mitigated circuits and variational optimization by injecting time-series covariates into fixed non-linear quantum dynamics and feeding measured expectation values to a classical linear readout.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A method that sidesteps error-correction needs offers a nearer-term commercial use for today's noisy processors.
insights.quote: injects time-series covariates into fixed, non-linear quantum dynamics and measures expectation values to construct high-dimensional feature representations

insights.claim: FirstQFM generated hardware-stabilized reservoir embeddings using 61 to 84 physical qubits across Rigetti's multi-chiplet processor.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows useful workloads running on a large fraction of a 108-qubit chiplet system.
insights.quote: utilizing 61 to 84 physical qubits across Rigetti’s multi-chiplet processor

insights.claim: The study positions QRC as a latency-efficient paradigm for deploying NISQ processors in quantitative finance.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quant finance could become an early paying vertical for NISQ hardware vendors.
insights.quote: the study establishes QRC as a latency-efficient paradigm for deploying NISQ processors in quantitative finance

insights.claim: FirstQFM's model disagreed with classical benchmarks on 49.0% of directional calls on average, and on days opposing the classical consensus it achieved a 50.89% win rate.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Low correlation with classical models suggests QRC signals could add diversification value in an ensemble even if standalone edge is thin.
insights.quote: on days where the QRC forecast opposed the majority consensus of the classical models, QRC achieved a 50.89% win rate

insights.claim: To eliminate lookahead bias and leakage, SW7 Group anonymized all features and asset identifiers across six expanding chronological training, validation and test folds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Blinded third-party validation raises credibility relative to typical vendor-run quantum finance claims.
insights.quote: anonymized all features and asset identifiers across six expanding chronological training, validation, and test folds

insights.claim: The authors explicitly disclaim general quantum advantage, acknowledging larger drawdowns accompanied the higher P&L and that classical simulability boundaries remain an evolving target.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Investors should not treat the result as proof of quantum advantage; risk-adjusted and cost-adjusted replication is still needed.
insights.quote: the authors explicitly disclaim general quantum advantage—acknowledging that larger drawdowns accompanied the higher P&L
